_comment_about_this_file: Per-document-type classifier hints for mgs_well_log. Loaded into document_types.classifier_hints via `node ai/scripts/set-classifier-hints.js --slug mgs_well_log --file ai/data/classifier-hints/mgs_well_log.json`. Edits land in the registry, get spliced into the visual classifier's system prompt for any page being evaluated against this slug, and override the generic page_purpose definitions when there's a conflict.
_iteration_notes: v1: caught permits (p2, p3, p6) but over-applied to the well plugging record (p7).
v2: replaced the 'permit form' framing with an explicit Application-vs-Record distinction.

v3 (this version): hints were never reaching the batched classifier (bug fixed in batchedVisualClassifier.js v5). Rewrote for the combined whitelist+blacklist approach. Added duplicate/summary page detection via cross-batch context.
keep_when: An actual MGS well log page has a TABULAR log structure — depth/elevation columns running down the page with formation or lithology descriptions per depth interval, well construction details (casing, screen, surface completion), or drilling progress entries. It is primarily a LOG of measurements and observations laid out in a grid or column format.

The mgs_well_log document type INCLUDES 'Well Plugging Record' pages (titles like 'Well Plugging Record', 'Record of Well Plugging'). These document HOW the well was plugged — cement intervals, plugging materials, depths sealed. They are DATA documents with extractable fields. Do NOT confuse a 'Well Plugging Record' (KEEP) with an 'Application for Permission to Abandon' (SKIP).
skip_when: APPLICATION and PERMIT forms — any page with a title containing 'Application for', 'Permit to', 'Permission to' (e.g., 'Application for Permit to Drill', 'Permit to Drill', 'Application for Permission to Abandon', 'Permit Granted'). These are administrative request/approval documents, NOT the well log itself. Classify as document_type_slug='none'. They may mention well data (location, depths, formations) but that data also appears on the actual log pages.

SUMMARY or DUPLICATE pages that RESTATE information already present on earlier pages in this document. If a page contains a condensed summary of drilling data, casing records, formation notes, or mud/operational details that REPEAT the same well's depth and formation information already visible on the primary log form (the full tabular grid pages), classify it as document_type_slug='none'. The primary log form with its full column layout is the authoritative source — shorter recap tables, casing run summaries, and operational notes that merely restate the same drilling data are redundant copies.

How to distinguish: the PRIMARY well log form has a detailed multi-row tabular grid (many depth intervals listed row by row). A SUMMARY/DUPLICATE page restates the same data in a shorter, less structured format — often a half-page of handwritten notes, a brief form with a few casing depths, or a condensed recap. When in doubt, check the RECORDS IDENTIFIED context: if an earlier page already captured the full tabular log for this well, a later page with the same well's data in condensed form is redundant.
